## {#workflow .beat-titles}

::: {.kicker}
The datom workflow
:::

::: {.beats}
[It starts with a programmer and a folder.]{.beat .fragment .fade-out data-fragment-index="1"}
[One call sets it up: code to git, data to storage.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="1"}
[Drop files in. Sync.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="2"}
[A second programmer clones the code, not the data.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="3"}
[Next month: one sync, three outcomes.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="4"}
[Readers read from storage alone.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="5"}
[A set is a project too.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="6"}
[A set is pointers to exact versions.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="7"}
[Derive, then release the set with its code.]{.beat .fragment .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="8"}
[Readers read a set the same way.]{.beat .fragment data-fragment-index="9"}
:::

::: notes
2:30 · 9 clicks

- 1 · One command: git repo + linked data store
- 2 · One sync: data + its record as code
- 3 · Clone: the code, not the data
- 4 · dm same, lb v2, ae new: one sync
- 5 · Read any table by version
- 6 · Product mode for derived data
- 7 · Sync links the study's tables, no copy → set v1
- 8 · R code + liver_flags → set v2; record in git, data in storage
- 9 · Reader pulls the set, fetches a member
:::
